info.title: spacecat DayZ mod → receiver ingest contract
info.description:
The contract a service must implement to receive live state **directly from the DayZ mod**, without the Node API in between.

UNKNOWN-VALUE CONVENTIONS — read this before writing a consumer. A numeric field the game cannot supply arrives as `-1` (never a reading); a string arrives as `""`; a whole object arrives as `null` or is omitted. A receiver must collapse **all three** to "unknown". Absence alone is NOT a reliable signal: Enforce's `JsonSerializer` writes every declared member of a class and cannot omit one per-instance, so a field that is meaningless for a given row still appears, carrying its sentinel. Treating `-1` as a value is how you end up rendering "Level -1" and a blank owner name.

ARRAY ABSENCE vs EMPTINESS is meaningful and distinct: a top-level array key that is **missing or null** means no source for it is registered at all (e.g. no territory mod installed, or AI collection switched off); a key **present and empty** means a source is active and reported zero rows. Consumers should surface those differently — otherwise a server running hundreds of AI silently looks identical to one with the feature disabled.

IMPORTANT — direction of flow: the DayZ Enforce mod is an HTTP *client* (its `RestApi` is outbound-only). It cannot be connected to. Instead it PUSHES data to, and POLLS commands from, whatever URL is set as `baseUrl` in the server's `$profile:spacecat/spacecat_api.json`. Point that at your service and implement the paths below, and your service becomes the receiver.

So in this document the request bodies are what the **mod sends you**, and the responses are what **your service must return**. Bind your service where the mod can reach it (the mod POSTs to `baseUrl`; the default is `http://127.0.0.1:4317`, i.e. the DayZ server host's loopback — co-locate, or set `baseUrl` to a reachable host).

Cadence: snapshot every `snapshotInterval` s (default 5), command poll every `commandPollInterval` s (default 2), catalog once after the first successful snapshot (chunked; re-sent on error). All requests carry `Content-Type: application/json`.

Minimal consumer (state only): implement `/ingest/snapshot` and `/ingest/catalog` returning 2xx, and `/ingest/commands` returning `{"commands":[]}`. You only need `/ingest/commands/ack` and non-empty command lists if you want to drive broadcast/kick/scanItems.

CRITICAL: `/ingest/snapshot` MUST return 2xx — the mod only sends the catalog after a snapshot POST succeeds. A non-2xx anywhere is treated by the mod as an error (it retries the catalog; snapshots simply resend next tick).

servers.description: Your service, at whatever host:port you set as the mod's baseUrl

tags.name: push
tags.description: The mod POSTs live state to you

tags.name: poll
tags.description: The mod pulls commands from you and reports results

post.summary: Receive a live snapshot (players, AI, territories, heartbeat + map)
post.description: Sent every snapshotInterval seconds. Contains the full current state; there is no delta — just replace your latest snapshot. MUST return 2xx (this is the mod's reachability probe that gates the catalog send).

200.description: Accepted. Body is ignored by the mod; any 2xx works.

post.summary: Receive a catalog chunk (config-derived type metadata)
post.description: Sent in chunks after the first successful snapshot. The first chunk of a fresh export has `reset: true` — clear your catalog then; subsequent chunks (`reset: false`) merge by `name`. Covers CfgVehicles/CfgWeapons/CfgMagazines. Return 2xx; a non-2xx un-latches delivery and the whole catalog is re-sent after the next snapshot (bounded to 5 attempts).

get.summary: Return pending commands for the mod to execute
get.description: Polled every commandPollInterval seconds. Return the commands you want the server to run since the last poll; return an empty array if none. Each command you return should be executed once — the mod does not de-dupe, so only return a command until it has been picked up. Command types: broadcast (in-game notification), kick (disconnect a player), scanItems (enumerate spawned items in a region; results come back via /ingest/commands/ack).

post.description: The mod calls this after executing a command. broadcast/kick send a string `result`; scanItems sends an `items` array (the region scan). Match on `id` to the command you issued. Return 2xx.

Ok.description: Any 2xx is fine; the mod ignores the response body of push/ack calls.

hands.description: Classname of the item in hands; absent or "" when empty-handed.

Weather.description: Present only when weather is available; each 0..1.

ServerInfo.description: Heartbeat. fps is present only when a frame timeslice is known; weather only when available.

online.description: REAL players only. Expansion AI and logged-out bodies still in the world are excluded — both are PlayerBase instances returned by GetGame().GetPlayers(), and counting them inflated this number before v1.1.0.

ai.description: AI characters detected this tick; 0 when detection is off. Ships alongside `online` so the drop in `online` at v1.1.0 is visibly accounted for.

AiInfo.description: One AI character. Field-for-field the same stat block as PlayerInfo (so both can render through one code path), plus AI identity. Written flat rather than as an allOf on PlayerInfo because PlayerInfo's `id`/`steamId` mean BI account ids, which an AI does not have. Same -1/"" conventions as everything else here.

id.description: Effectively REQUIRED, and stable for the entity's lifetime — the mod sends "<netLow>:<netHigh>". This is the map marker key and the selection id; fall back to an array index and the selected AI changes under the admin's cursor on every poll.

name.description: Display name; "" means the receiver should substitute `cls` or a generic label.

faction.description: Expansion AI faction; "" without the AI compat PBO.

group.description: Patrol/group name; "" without the AI compat PBO.

energy.description: -1 when the engine never declared the stat.

source.description: Which classifier answered. "expansion" is an exact eAIBase cast from the AI compat PBO; "heuristic" is the core's classname-prefix fallback, which is close but not authoritative. Surface the difference rather than hiding it.

TerritoryMember.description: One territory roster entry. `rank` and `permissions` are mutually exclusive in practice — Expansion has ranks, BasicTerritories has a permission bitmask — and NEITHER is guaranteed.

id.description: Effectively REQUIRED, and the only value guaranteed present: the BI GUID (PlayerIdentity.GetId()), which is what BOTH territory systems persist. NOT a steam64.

steamId.description: Resolved from the mod's persistent GUID ledger. "" when that GUID has never been seen logging in.

name.description: The territory system's own cached name where it has one (Expansion), else the ledger name. "" when unresolvable — the receiver should then fall back to showing `id`.

rank.description: Plain word, never a #STR_ localisation key (a dedicated server has no localisation table). "" under a system with no ranks.

permissions.description: BasicTerritories permission bitmask; -1 under a system with no such concept.

permissionNames.description: The bitmask already decoded into words, e.g. ["build","dismantle"]. Decoded mod-side, using the territory mod's OWN constants — the bit layout is that mod's private ABI, so a receiver that hard-codes the numbers silently mis-renders every roster after a version bump. Prefer these over `permissions`.

online.description: This GUID is connected right now. Arrives as 1/0 (Enforce bool).

TerritoryInfo.description: One territory flag. Two territory systems can be live at once and expose different things, so this is ONE shape with per-field sentinels rather than a union: a field the registering system cannot supply carries "" or -1. `pos` is the only field that must be usable — a row without it cannot be placed on a map and should be dropped.

key.description: "<round(x)>_<round(z)>". Position-derived, so it is stable across server restarts — unlike any script handle. Use it to correlate rows between polls.

system.description: The system that filled ownership/roster below. "" means NO territory compat answered — the row still carries real vanilla flag state, but nothing is claimed about ownership.

systems.description: Every compat that contributed. Normally one entry; more only if a flag is registered in both systems, in which case field-level first-writer-wins applies.

ownerId.description: BI GUID; "" when unclaimed or no system answered.

ownerSteamId.description: "" when the ledger could not resolve it.

claimed.description: A territory system reports a non-empty owner. Arrives as 1/0.

name.description: Territory name. "" under BasicTerritories, which has no such concept — not a gap, the honest answer.

level.description: Expansion territory level; -1 under BasicTerritories. NOT the same thing as flag charge — see refresher01.

memberCount.description: Roster size BEFORE any cap, and always excluding the owner. Normalised mod-side because the two systems disagree: Expansion's NumberOfMembers() includes the owner and BasicTerritories' excludes it. -1 when no system answered.

members.description: Never includes the owner. May be shorter than memberCount — see membersTruncated.

membersTruncated.description: The roster was longer than the mod's territoryMaxMembers cap. Arrives as 1/0. Without this a capped roster is indistinguishable from a small one.

refresher01.description: Flag refresher charge, 0..1 (vanilla, always available). Multiply by 100 for the percentage the in-game flag shows.

objects.description: Base-building objects inside the territory radius, counted by the mod itself (GetObjectsAtPosition3D + IsRefresherSignalingViable). -1 means NEVER SCANNED, which is emphatically not the same as 0 — render it as unknown.

cargo.description: Cargo items across those objects. Same -1/0 distinction.

radius.description: Radius the counts were taken at, metres; -1 when never scanned. Worth preferring over a server-wide setting when two territory mods with different sizes are live.

scanAge.description: Seconds since that scan; -1 when never scanned. Counts are refreshed on a budgeted round-robin, NOT per snapshot, so they are deliberately allowed to be stale — this is how stale.

WorldMap.description: Live positions. vehicles/events are empty arrays in v1; players and ai populate.

Snapshot.description: Full current live state; sent whole each tick (no deltas).

ai.description: Expansion AI characters. ABSENT/null when AI collection is switched off; PRESENT AND EMPTY when detection ran and found none. Whole-state replacement each tick, like players — a receiver must CLEAR this layer when the mod goes stale rather than holding the last known list, or dead bots haunt the map after a game-server restart.

territories.description: One row per territory flag in the world. ABSENT/null when territory collection is switched off; PRESENT AND EMPTY when it ran and there are no flags. Rows appear even with no territory mod installed (carrying vanilla flag state and system:"").

TypeDetail.description: One catalog entry. inventorySlot = slots this item occupies; attachments = slots this object exposes.

displayName.description: Localized English name ($UNT$ / untranslated entries are excluded by the mod).

magazines.description: Compatible magazine classes (CfgWeapons magazines[]); empty for non-weapons.

cargoSize.description: Its own cargo grid as [width, height]; empty when the class declares none.

isContainer.description: 1 if the class descends from Container_Base/DeployableContainer_Base; holds cargo even when itemsCargoSize is absent (grid lives in the p3d). The mod's Enforce JsonSerializer emits bool as 1/0.

isDeployable.description: 1 if the class can be placed/deployed into the world (base-building kits, tents, traps, fireplaces, garden plots, deployable containers). Used to scope Expansion base-building deployable pickers. The mod's Enforce JsonSerializer emits bool as 1/0.

hitpoints.description: Base durability (DamageSystem GlobalHealth Health hitpoints); 0 if none.

armor.description: DamageSystem GlobalArmor, one row per declared damage-type (cfgAmmo class). damage is what that type deals to the zone: 0 = immune, higher = less protection.

ArmorEntry.description: One GlobalArmor damage-type row. Zone value is -1 when that zone isn't declared (distinct from a declared 0 = full immunity).

ammo.description: cfgAmmo/damage-type class name (e.g. Bullet_762x39, FragGrenade, MeleeFist).

health.description: Health-zone damage coefficient; -1 if not declared.

blood.description: Blood-zone damage coefficient; -1 if not declared.

shock.description: Shock-zone damage coefficient; -1 if not declared.

reset.description: true on the first chunk of a fresh export — clear your catalog before merging.

CommandArgs.description: Only the fields relevant to the command type are meaningful.

x.description: scanItems: world X of sweep centre.

z.description: scanItems: world Z of sweep centre.

radius.description: scanItems: sphere radius (m); mod caps at 200.

id.description: Your correlation id; echoed back in the ack.

ItemInfo.description: A spawned world item from a scanItems sweep.

lifetimeMax.description: Configured CE lifetime (s); live remaining TTL is not exposed by the engine.

ScanAck.description: Ack for scanItems — the region scan result.
